blurb: `Wire(…)` delivers raw text to an http body or path segment. A queue message, a cron tick, an `on call` or an event has no raw text form: it is a typed value, and `Wire` would hand it to a typed decoder as a string and fail confusingly at run time. Pass the typed value. To drive an http route with raw text, see `bynk.test.wire_needs_system`.
summary: A `Wire(...)` raw argument is passed to a queue, cron, `on call` or event address; `Wire` drives an http body or path segment only, so a queue message, cron tick or event is passed as a typed value.
